images.prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama. A compact desk printer about the size of a shoebox stands on a slim graphite cart with four small castors at the centre of a pale neutral tabletop. Its casing is matte graphite with chamfered corners and a frosted acrylic output tray. A single ivory sheet is jammed half out of the feed slot, crumpled into an accordion. The one acid-lime element is the small status lamp on the top panel, glowing to flag the jam. Behind the cart, a strip of pale ivory card runs to the back edge as a miniature pathway, and at the far right a patch of ivory paper grass, cut into thin fringed strips, marks an open field. Grey toner dust coats the tray lip, and the castors show faint scuffs. Wide 16:9 landscape frame. The hero object sits slightly left of centre on the lower third, with the related objects extending to the right so the workflow reads left to right. Clean, generous negative space above. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: one large soft key light from the upper left at about 45 degrees, like diffused north-window daylight, with a gentle white bounce fill from the right; soft grounded contact shadows fall to the lower right. Camera: 100mm macro lens at f/4, eye level with the tabletop, three-quarter view. The hero object is tack sharp and the background melts into smooth, creamy blur on a seamless pale neutral sweep. Mood: calm, precise, orderly and quietly premium, like high-end editorial product photography. Strictly no people, figures, faces, hands or silhouettes. No readable text, letters, numbers, clock digits, logos, signage or user-interface graphics anywhere. No holograms, floating screens, robots with faces, dense cable tangles, carnival or circus elements, cartoon or plastic CGI look, oversaturated colour, lens flare or heavy vignette.

Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama, captured mid-disaster. The same cart has rolled along the ivory pathway and stopped at the edge of the paper-grass field, one castor snagged in the fringe and the cart pitching forward. The printer has slid off and landed on its side in the grass, lid sprung open, its frosted output tray snapped and lying a short span away. The jammed sheet has finally torn free and hangs frozen in the air above it, with a burst of loose ivory pages from the feeder fanning back toward the pathway. A cloud of grey toner dust hangs over the impact point, and small graphite screws and a roller spring lie scattered in an arc. The lime status lamp still glows from the upturned panel. Wide 16:9 landscape frame, same layout and angle as the calm version of this scene. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: the same soft upper-left key and right-side bounce fill as a calm studio setup, unchanged, so the disorder reads as physical and real rather than theatrical. Airborne paper, grains and fragments catch the key light with crisp edge highlights. Camera: 85mm lens at f/5.6, same three-quarter tabletop angle, fast shutter freezing everything mid-air. Printer fragments lie scattered across it at building scale: a cracked graphite side panel standing upright like a wall, a split frosted tray bleached white, snapped rollers half sunk in the ground like fallen columns. Torn pages have weathered into pale sediment between the tufts. In the midground, a slim graphite rail sled runs on two thin tracks between a set of rebuilt feed rollers, and its acid-lime guide rollers are threading one clean sheet from a restored input tray through to a new frosted output tray, a single complete paper path running straight across the ruin. Wide 16:9 panoramic frame. The main ruin anchors the left or centre foreground, terrain rolls back to a distant horizon on the upper third, and the lime recovery rig sits in the right midground. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents.
